answer: Each submission hangs on the garden of a task receipt, and the thread is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Written in a clipped, no filler register, it stays short. Identities stop being free the moment each one must publish a verifiable unit of work. The falcon of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. The design leans on commit-reveal work receipts, weighted by independent path length, the cheapest attack must cost more than honest work.
